intent.subject: Shalabi (C-01), face in three-quarter view, readable but held in darkness by red-filtered light and starlight.
intent.action: He points along the newly chosen compass bearing and quietly states that the enemy waits on the known route, reclaiming the initiative.
intent.setting: The marshy Tina Plain at LOC-0003, with darkness beyond his gesture.

research.claim: The company is shown beginning its march through the Tina Plain/marsh after the early helicopter drop.
research.note: Follows production decision D-1 to use the Egyptian account of the early Tina Plain drop and long march; the landing location and march distance remain disputed and require the episode end-card source note.

research.claim: The precise setting of this first-march moment as full night is not explicitly established in the ledger.
research.note: H-05 and H-08 support the drop and march, but do not establish this beat's exact time of night.

research.claim: Composite Corporal Mahmoud sends/receives and decodes the coded radio traffic, warns Shalabi that the signal was intercepted, worries about losing contact with command, and switches off the set.
research.note: Mahmoud is a composite character. His actions dramatize the sourced intercepted-signal and radio-silence event without assigning it to a documented real individual.

research.claim: Captain Hamdi Shalabi orders radio silence after the intercepted-signal warning.
research.note: The coded warning and Shalabi's radio-silence order are stated by the primary Egyptian account; the marked dialogue is a permitted dramatized paraphrase.

research.claim: Shalabi taps the switched-off radio and draws a finger across his lips to communicate the sourced radio-silence order; the file passes the silent signal back man to man.
research.note: Permitted staging under P-01: the gestures visually show the sourced radio-silence order and add no new event or outcome.

research.claim: Composite Sergeant Sayed hears the silence order and asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
research.note: Sayed is a composite character; the question is fictional character dialogue and does not credit him with a documented act.

research.claim: Shalabi uses his compass, changes the file's bearing, and directs the company toward an unexpected approach after the interception warning.
research.note: The route-change dialogue is an approved paraphrase of the source treatment that the enemy did not expect anyone to come from that direction. The compass and turning-file business are permitted P-01 staging.

research.claim: The Soviet-pattern manpack radio, whip antenna, handset placement, and use of red light are presented as period equipment/detail.
research.note: The ledger documents radio traffic and silence, but does not source this specific radio model/configuration or red-light procedure.

flags.detail: The beat fixes the company's first steps into the marsh at night, but the ledger does not establish the exact time for this moment.
The specific Soviet-pattern manpack radio configuration, whip antenna, handset placement, and red-light decoding procedure are not sourced in the ledger.

direction.coverage: Begin in a shadowed medium close-up, then hold as his pointing arm leads into a dark over-the-shoulder bearing view.
direction.blocking: Shalabi stands still at the marsh edge, turns three-quarters toward camera, and extends one deliberate arm into the unlit plain.
direction.performance_note: Deliver the line low and certain, with no flourish—authority returning through calm precision.
direction.pacing: A measured pause before the gesture, then a clean, decisive hold in silence.
direction.tone_ref: Restrained historical war realism: red-filtered command-post darkness, cold starlight, and oppressive empty terrain.

wardrobe.additions: Egyptian captain's rank: exactly three small gold five-pointed stars in a row on each plain khaki shoulder strap, plain khaki collar with no collar tabs or badges, compass on a lanyard (PRP-0008)
visible_details: Bare head with short, damp black hair; no headgear
Sand-khaki 1973 cotton field jacket, rolled to forearms, with two buttoned chest pockets
Soviet-pattern khaki canvas chest rig: three closed-flap magazine pouches, plain cotton straps, simple metal buckles
Exactly three small gold five-pointed captain’s stars in a row on the near plain-khaki shoulder strap; plain collar with no tabs or badges
PRP-0008 compass remains on its lanyard at his chest or controlled in the non-pointing hand, readable as the newly used navigation tool
Wet jacket splashes and dark brine-and-mud staining on trousers above the knees; black leather boots only implied at this MCU scale
No modern kit, helmet, body armor, flag patch, chest eagle, or visible text
wardrobe.notes: Continue directly from 2.4-05: same mud-wet uniform and damp bare-headed appearance. At MCU, prioritize captain stars, lanyarded compass, period canvas rig, rolled sleeves, and wet fabric sheen; his extended pointing arm must not obscure the rank or chest rig.

makeup.skin_state: Medium-olive face cold-damp with sweat and brine sheen across brow, nose, cheekbones and exposed ear; sparse dark mud flecks at jawline, neck and lower cheeks; restrained fatigue shadows beneath narrow eyes. Mud-splashed hands and rolled forearms, with red-filtered light catching the wet sheen while cold starlight leaves the far cheek in shadow.
makeup.hair_state: Bare-headed short black hair remains neatly side-parted, wet and lightly flattened at the crown; a few damp strands cling at the high forehead. Thin upturned handlebar mustache is damp and exact in shape.
makeup.notes: Keep his long narrow face, hollow cheeks, intense dark-brown eyes and signature mustache fully recognizable in three-quarter profile; no blood, wounds, or heavy grime that obscures lip-sync.

dressing: Thin broken white salt crust over black mud at the firmer marsh edge
Shallow mid-shin brine sheets with faint cold sky reflections and halted boot prints
Fresh arcing turn tracks disappearing into the unlit flat
Sparse low salt-marsh scrub silhouettes, with no landmarks to the horizon
A period metal flashlight fitted with a red filter, held low by an unseen Egyptian commando immediately camera-right and just behind Shalabi; kept outside the MCU frame
set.set_state: Shalabi stands on a firmer salt-crust edge above shallow mid-shin brine, actively using PRP-0008 while the halted column's wet prints and abrupt route-change track remain visible behind him.
set.notes: The unseen operator aims the red-filtered flashlight upward from camera-right at Shalabi’s lower cheek, jaw, and pointing-side forearm, creating a localized restrained red glow while cold moonlight and starlight retain the dark blue-black marsh and a thin wet rim; no visible practical enters frame.

camera.light: Cold blue-black moon and starlight remain the dominant high rear-side key from camera-left, giving a thin wet rim and faint broken reflections. Coordinate with Set to place a hooded red-filtered flashlight just below and camera-right at the frame edge, angled up toward Shalabi’s near cheek and mouth; its muted red side/up-light stays tightly localized and falls away before his extended arm and the empty plain.
camera.exposure_note: Hold the marsh and background 2–3 stops under Shalabi’s moonlit rim; expose the localized red practical only enough to retain natural skin texture, clear eyes and lip-sync mouth movement without lifting the surrounding black-blue night.
camera.framing_note: Generate 16:9 for the 2.39:1 crop: keep Shalabi’s three-quarter face, eyes, speaking mouth, compass lanyard, and pointing hand within the central middle 75% height band. Let the arm lead toward frame-right darkness while preserving an unbroken dark bearing beyond the gesture.

action.choreography: Shalabi holds steady at the marsh edge, pauses after the off-screen hand sign, then turns his torso three-quarters and makes one controlled, low-forward pointing gesture into the darkness while delivering the line. His compass remains as the locked lanyard costume prop, settling against his chest rig without being raised or manipulated.
action.movement: Stationary, balanced stance in shallow mid-shin brine and mud; no step, splash, or wading action during the 7-second hold.
beats: One deliberate arm extends on the new bearing
Holds the pointing line into darkness
action.safety_note: Keep the footing planted on the firmer marsh edge; shallow brine remains mid-shin and the gesture does not disturb the water.

reasons: The intent identifies the subject (Shalabi/C-01), his decisive action, the Tina Plain setting with LOC-0003, night time of day, and a controlled tactical mood.
It preserves the beat's key dramatic action: Shalabi establishes a new compass bearing and redirects the force away from the route the enemy expects.
All referenced library-backed elements included in the intent are identified: C-01 and LOC-0003. The radio prop is appropriately referenced from the stated asset list.
The wording does not introduce unsupported historical facts; 'reclaiming the initiative' is a thematic framing of the documented rerouting decision.
Coverage, blocking, performance note, pacing, and tone reference are all explicitly present.
The blocking preserves Shalabi's three-quarter readability while keeping the gesture directed into darkness, matching the night-marsh staging and tactical intent.
The low, certain delivery and measured pause support a tense, controlled reclaiming of initiative without melodrama.
The restrained historical-war realism, red-filtered light, starlight, and empty terrain are consistent with the requested grounded tone.

The shot’s readable red-filtered facial light is motivated by a flashlight, but Set places no red-filtered flashlight or specifies an off-screen practical/source position. This leaves the camera department’s stated localized red glow without a placed set element, contrary to the requirement that a prop motivating light be placed by Set.
revise_instructions: Add a period-plausible red-filtered flashlight as a specifically placed off-screen or edge-of-frame practical source, with its operator/location defined so it can cast the localized low upward-side red glow on Shalabi while remaining unseen in the MCU. Do not add it as a new carried prop for Shalabi; PRP-0008 remains his locked carried compass.

reasons: The camera lighting plan relies on a localized red-filtered flashlight glow, but the Set output does not place or motivate that practical source. The source must be concretely coordinated with Set before this lighting instruction is production-ready.
revise_instructions: After Set defines the off-screen/edge-of-frame red-filtered flashlight placement, specify that the muted red side/up-light is cast from that exact practical position and remains localized to Shalabi’s readable face and mouth. Preserve the moon/starlight-dominant low-key exposure and darkness beyond the gesture.
